newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Escudo steady after Thursday's fall vs mark.
newsitem.headline: Escudo steady after Thursday's fall vs mark.

text.p: The escudo was steady around the weaker levels to which it slipped against the mark on Thursday with the possibility that the Bank of Portugal could intervene helping to hold the line, traders said.
The currency was trading at 100.84/87 to the mark against its 100.86/91 close on Thursday.
Traders said that if the currency approached 101.00 then the Bank could step in to prevent a further weakening.
But they added that if the same reasoning applied to explain Thursday's fall was valid, then there was scope for further declines in the escudo-mark rate.

With Portugal and Spain having similar interest rate levels, it made sense for the currencies to enter the single currency -- for which they are both now seen as prime candidates -- at around their mid-point in the European Monetary System grid.
The mid-point for peseta-escudo is 1.2049 escudos to the peseta but the rate currently stands at 1.1955/62.
In the EMS grid, the escudo is the second strongest currency, standing 2.05 percent above the weakest member, the French franc.
